section: India - agriculture: major food crops (rice, wheat, maize, pulses) and their regions
subsections: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season
Shifting cultivation in India - local names → state
Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months
Food grain production trends - rice/wheat output, world rank, exports

accepted.s: Which one of the following cereals ranks first in India in terms of importance and is a staple food for more than half of the country's population?
accepted.x: Rice is the first-ranking cereal in India and is the staple food of more than half of the country's population.
accepted.tq: Use the rank and population-share clue to identify the cereal.
accepted.sec: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the cultivation of rice in India, consider the following statements:
1. Rice requires high humidity.
2. A temperature above 25°C is considered ideal for rice.
3. Rice requires more than 100 cm of rainfall, though irrigation can compensate for inadequate rainfall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rice grows best under high humidity, temperatures above 25°C and rainfall exceeding 100 cm, or equivalent irrigation.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of climatic requirements by checking each statement independently.
accepted.sec: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rice is especially suited to which of the following soil and geographical environments?
o: Clayey or loamy soils of deltaic and coastal alluvial areas
Laterite soils of upland plateaus only
accepted.x: Rice is well suited to clayey or loamy soils, particularly the deltaic and coastal alluvium.
accepted.tq: Match the crop with its characteristic soil and landform.
accepted.sec: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding wheat cultivation in India is NOT correct?
o: It requires a cool growing season and bright warm sunshine at the time of ripening.
It is mainly a rabi crop.
Wheat is the second most important cereal in India.
The black-soil region of the Deccan is unsuitable for wheat cultivation.
accepted.x: The statement is NOT correct. Wheat is grown not only in the Ganga-Satluj plains but also in the black-soil region of the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed suitability statement, especially where a known crop-soil association is denied.
accepted.sec: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The annual rainfall requirement generally associated with wheat cultivation in India is:
accepted.x: Wheat generally requires about 50–75 cm of rainfall and is also supported by irrigation in major producing regions.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct numerical range from four distinct rainfall bands.
accepted.sec: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pulses — high-moisture crop requiring continuous heavy rainfall
Millets — mainly kharif crops suited to dryland and rainfed tracts
Wheat — crop of hot and humid monsoon season
Rice — crop requiring low-input dryland conditions
accepted.x: Millets are mostly kharif crops and are climate-resilient, low-input crops of dryland and rainfed tracts.
accepted.tq: Eliminate pairs that reverse the characteristic climate or season of the crop.
accepted.sec: Growth conditions - rank among cereals, temperature, rainfall, soil, season  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs of local name and region of shifting cultivation is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Milpa is the name of shifting cultivation in Mexico. Bastar is associated with Dipa.
accepted.tq: Use the location trap by distinguishing Indian regional names from foreign names.
accepted.sec: Shifting cultivation in India - local names → state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Dipa, as a local name for shifting cultivation, is associated with which of the following regions?
accepted.x: Dipa is associated with Bastar in Chhattisgarh and the Andaman region.
accepted.tq: Directly test a region-name association from a closely confusable list.
accepted.sec: Shifting cultivation in India - local names → state  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Pama Dabi — Odisha
2. Koman — Odisha
3. Bringa — Odisha
4. Ponam — Kerala
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Pama Dabi, Koman and Bringa are names used in Odisha, while Ponam or Poonam is associated with Kerala.
accepted.tq: Check every regional synonym before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Shifting cultivation in India - local names → state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to shifting cultivation outside India?
accepted.x: Ladang is associated with Malaysia and Indonesia. Milpa is associated with Mexico, Roca with Brazil, Chena with Sri Lanka and Taungya with Myanmar.
accepted.tq: Separate similar foreign regional names by using the location clue.
accepted.sec: Shifting cultivation in India - local names → state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes dryland agriculture?
o: Irrigated cultivation receiving more than 150 cm rainfall
Rainfed cultivation generally receiving less than 75 cm rainfall, with millets and pulses as important crops
Deltaic cultivation of rice under standing water
Winter cultivation dependent exclusively on western disturbances
accepted.x: Dryland agriculture is rainfed, generally occurs where rainfall is below 75 cm, and commonly includes millets and pulses.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to a realistic set of rainfall and crop conditions.
accepted.sec: Shifting cultivation in India - local names → state  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following cropping seasons in the order of their usual sowing period, from earliest to latest:
A. Zaid
B. Rabi
C. Kharif
D. Zaid Kharif
accepted.x: Rabi sowing occurs from October to December, kharif from June to July, zaid kharif from August to September, and zaid from March to June. Considering the annual cycle beginning with the October–December sowing period, the listed order is Rabi, Kharif, Zaid Kharif and Zaid.
accepted.tq: Arrange the seasons by comparing their stated sowing windows.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the usual sowing and harvesting periods of kharif crops?
o: Sowing in March–June; harvesting in June–July
Sowing in October–December; harvesting in March–May
Sowing in June–July; harvesting in September–October or October–November
Sowing in August–September; harvesting in April–May
accepted.x: Kharif crops are generally sown in June–July with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested from September to November.
accepted.tq: Match a season with both its sowing and harvesting windows.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a usual rabi crop?
accepted.x: Jute is a kharif crop. Wheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas, linseed and potato are associated with the rabi season.
accepted.tq: Find the crop belonging to the neighbouring season rather than the season named.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The zaid season in India is generally characterised by which of the following?
o: A monsoon season beginning in June and ending in October
A rainfed season restricted to areas receiving less than 25 cm rainfall
A long winter season dependent on western disturbances
A short, irrigation-dependent summer window from March to June
accepted.x: Zaid is the short summer cropping window, generally extending from March to June, and it depends substantially on irrigation.
accepted.tq: Identify the season from its duration and irrigation requirement.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of common zaid crops?
accepted.x: Watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder are important crops of the zaid season.
accepted.tq: Use the all-crops group to identify the season-specific list.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the relationship between crops and seasons is correct?
o: Moong and urad can be cultivated in both seasons.
Millets are exclusively rabi crops throughout India.
Groundnut is restricted to the rabi season.
Potato is listed only as a kharif crop.
accepted.x: Moong and urad can be grown in more than one season. Groundnut can also be a both-season crop, while millets are mainly kharif with some southern rabi cultivation.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to the usual one-season classification.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rabi crops in India are supported by which combination of factors?
o: South-west monsoon rainfall and coastal humidity only
North-east monsoon alone and high summer temperatures
accepted.x: Rabi crops benefit from winter rainfall brought by western disturbances and from irrigation.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct climatic source and supplementary input for the season.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following represents the crop sequence classified as Zaid Kharif?
accepted.x: Zaid Kharif is associated with sowing in August–September and includes rapeseed and oilseeds, harvested around December–January.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two zaid subcategories by their crop lists and months.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid: crops and months  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding recent foodgrain production in India is correct?
o: Foodgrain production reached a record 357.73 million tonnes in 2024–25.
Foodgrain production in 2024–25 remained below 250 million tonnes.
Foodgrain production was exactly equal to horticulture production in 2024–25.
Horticulture production was lower than foodgrain production in 2024–25.
accepted.x: India recorded 357.73 million tonnes of foodgrain production in 2024–25. Horticulture production was higher at 367.72 million tonnes.
accepted.tq: Select the precise current figure while rejecting changed or reversed comparisons.
accepted.sec: Food grain production trends - rice/wheat output, world rank, exports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's rice production and world position, as stated for the recent period, are correctly represented by which of the following?
o: About 150.18 MT; first in the world, surpassing China
About 117.94 MT; first in the world
About 18.59 MT; second in the world after China
About 145.28 MT; second in the world after China
accepted.x: India's rice production is stated as about 150.18 MT, placing it first in the world and ahead of China's 145.28 MT.
accepted.tq: Combine the output figure with the ranking rather than treating either clue alone.
accepted.sec: Food grain production trends - rice/wheat output, world rank, exports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India accounts for approximately what share of world rice trade and is described as which type of rice trader?
o: About 60 per cent; the largest rice importer
About 10 per cent; the second-largest importer
About 25 per cent; a marginal exporter
About 40 per cent; the largest rice exporter
accepted.x: India is described as the largest rice exporter and accounts for approximately 40 per cent of world rice trade.
accepted.tq: Use the percentage and the trade rank together to avoid a producer-exporter reversal.
accepted.sec: Food grain production trends - rice/wheat output, world rank, exports  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's recent position in global wheat production?
o: Production of 150.18 MMT and first position in the world
Production of 117.94 MMT and second position in the world
Production of 18.59 MMT and second position in the world
Production of 145.28 MMT and third position in the world
accepted.x: India's wheat production is stated as 117.94 MMT, placing it second in the world.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among crop-specific output figures and rankings.
accepted.sec: Food grain production trends - rice/wheat output, world rank, exports  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding millets in India:
1. India is the largest millet producer in the world.
2. India's millet production is stated as 18.59 million tonnes.
3. India contributes 42.75 per cent of world millet output.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: India's millet production is 18.59 million tonnes, it is the world's largest millet producer, and its share is stated as 42.75 per cent.
accepted.tq: Verify the rank, absolute output and global share as separate statements.
accepted.sec: Food grain production trends - rice/wheat output, world rank, exports  [APPSC]
